judged_text: createEvent now takes both an externalId parameter and returns credentialId/externalId, but Google's createEvent ignores the externalId argument and re-derives the calendar by matching credentialId against destinationCalendar — two parallel sources of truth for the same fact. The next contributor must keep the credentialId-based lookup in GoogleCalendarService and the externalId threading through CalendarManager in sync; if a credential owns multiple calendars the two mechanisms disagree silently.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `CalendarManager.createEvent(credential, calEvent, externalId?)` returns `externalId` (used later by `EventManager` as `externalCalendarId`), but it never passes that `externalId` into the calendar integration; instead it calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts). In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the actual `calendarId` is chosen via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), i.e., derived from `credentialId` and the *first* matching destinationCalendar entry. If `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple calendars under the same credential (now plausible since destinationCalendar is an array), the loop in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` passes different `destination.externalId` values into `CalendarManager.createEvent`, but Google will still pick the first matching externalId, causing the stored `externalId` in the result to potentially not match where the event was actually created, breaking later update/delete via `externalCalendarId`.
